headlines.summary: As crypto evolves past its trading roots, and global markets shift to 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure.
headlines.article_text: Ripple strikes deal with Robinhood to expand its RLUD digital dollar Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Ripple has struck a deal with Robinhood to expand the use of Ripple's digital dollar, RLUSD, broadening trading and financing options for institutional clients and improving Robinhood's internal money management. The partnership meets Robinhood's ambition of becoming a global financial super-app, centralizing more of its customers' financial lives while expanding the underlying infrastructure that can serve both retail and institutional clients. As the crypto industry evolves beyond trading and markets shift to 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure. In this article HOOD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Ripple (L) and Robinhood (R) Getty Images Ripple has struck a deal with Robinhood to expand the reach of its digital dollar, RLUSD , strengthening trading and financing links between their institutional businesses and improving Robinhood's internal money management. The partnership involves using RLUSD to settle institutional trades, automate Robinhood's treasury operations and expand access to digital asset trading and financing through Ripple Prime and Bitstamp, the global crypto exchange acquired by Robinhood last year . It also helps meet Robinhood's ambition of becoming a global financial super-app, centralizing its customers' financial lives while expanding the underlying infrastructure that can serve both retail and institutional clients. "Utility is what moves stablecoins forward. Working with Ripple, Bitstamp and Robinhood will have access to RLUSD for institutional settlement, Ripple Treasury for our operations and Ripple Prime for financing," Robinhood Crypto general manager Johann Kerbrat said in a statement shared with CNBC. "That is what a connected, global financial system looks like." Workhorse Stablecoins have long been a workhorse of the crypto world, giving traders a way to move money among exchanges, buy and sell crypto assets, and park funds between trades without having to convert back into traditional currency. But as the crypto industry evolves beyond trading and markets move toward 24/7 liquidity, stablecoins are becoming essential financial infrastructure because of their ability to enable near-instant settlement and move dollar-denominated value at any time, regardless of traditional banking hours. As firms look to do more with stablecoins beyond simply listing them on exchanges, stablecoin issuers are betting they'll favor a one-stop-shop approach that bundles the technology and services needed to move money, settle trades and manage cash. "Stablecoins have evolved from a crypto trading tool into a critical piece of financial infrastructure," Ripple President Monica Long told CNBC. "The clearest evidence of this is where they're now being embedded — from corporate payments to capital markets. Our partnership with Robinhood reflects that evolution." "This is about much more than trading," she added. "It's about fundamentally changing how money moves and is managed – giving institutions the ability to operate 24/7/365, unlocking liquidity and putting capital to work more efficiently." Circle Internet Group, a Ripple competitor, is positioning itself for a similar future, where winning platforms, in addition to issuing stablecoins, also provide the infrastructure to put them to work. Earlier this year, for example, it launched the Circle Payments Network, connecting financial institutions and payment providers using its flagship USDC stablecoin and other digital assets for cross-border payments. The network is Circle's answer to the eight-year-old Ripple Payments business, a service that helps businesses move money across borders, using any of several assets moving through that system, including USDC, Ripple-created XRP and, as of its debut in December 2024, RLUSD. RLUSD's market cap has grown to more than $2.5 billion . Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC still dominate the total stablecoin market, which now exceeds $300 billion . RLUSD will also be listed on Robinhood's trading platform, and is currently available to traders on Bitstamp as well as Robinhood Chain, the company's home-grown blockchain for tokenized stocks and other assets. headlines.article_text: Boeing (BA) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Boeing narrowed its loss in the third quarter after defense sales rose. The company beat revenue expectations but posted a bigger loss per share than expected. Boeing executives will host an earnings conference call at 10:30 a.m. ET. In this article BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT VIDEO 6:41 06:41 Watch CNBC's full interview with Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg Boeing narrowed its loss in the third quarter after defense sales rose, but CEO Kelly Ortberg told staff that the manufacturer has "more work to do." For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program. Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion. Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG: Loss per share: 34 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 21 cents expected Revenue: $24.19 billion vs $23.84 billion expected. Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier. Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said. Stabilizing production The company is working on stabilizing production of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft, work that will likely continue through this year , Ortberg reiterated Tuesday. "I know everybody wants us to go faster but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday. Boeing has been producing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month, but is aiming for more. "Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality." Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it. Certification wins The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet. And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line. Bruce Bennett | Getty Images JetBlue Airways reported a bigger loss in the third quarter compared with last year, but the New York carrier said strong travel demand is helping to offset higher fuel prices as it seeks to calm investors after shares fell to a new low Monday. JetBlue stock was up nearly 15% in premarket trading Tuesday. JetBlue on Monday posted a net loss of $257 million for the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with a loss of $143 million a year earlier. The carrier's fuel bill rose 61% to $868 million. "Resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue well ahead of our initial expectations, allowing us to recapture more of the increase in fuel costs than we initially expected," CEO Joanna Geraghty said in an earnings release. "That momentum has carried into the fourth quarter, and Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver exceptional results even as we significantly grow capacity." JetBlue's average fares rose more than 19% to $245.11 in the third quarter from $205.67 in the year-earlier period. JetBlue executives are set to hold an earnings call on Tuesday at 10 a.m. ET, where they will face questions from analysts about the company's long-term health amid sustained losses. A group of the airline's senior creditors is reportedly working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners , the Wall Street Journal reported Friday. The airline said its revenue per available seat mile, a key metric measuring how much operating revenue a carrier generates for every seat flown one mile, would be up as much as 22% in the fourth quarter, bringing the annual increase to an expected 13.5% to 14.5% The carrier said it ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity and that its unencumbered asset base is now $7 billion, including $2.8 billion in aircraft and engines. JetBlue had total debt of $8.4 billion as of Sept. 30, the carrier said in its earnings filing Monday. "Importantly, we believe we have the liquidity and financing options to create a strong bridge to at least $1 EPS and positive free cash flow in 2028," CFO Ursula Hurley said in a statement. "We remain focused on disciplined cost execution and capital management as we work toward sustained profitability and positive free cash flow." Here is what JetBlue reported in the third quarter compared with Wall Street estimates compiled by LSEG: Loss per share: 60 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 55 cents expected Revenue: $2.81 billion vs. $2.82 billion expected JetBlue last posted an annual profit in 2019. The airline is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan that includes cutting cuts and boosting revenue by investing in premium seats, like a new domestic first class section that recently went on sale. Fuel costs have eaten into airline profits across the board. JetBlue said travel demand has remained strong despite higher fares , which are up more than 20% this year. JetBlue has struggled not just with higher costs but also with competition from larger rivals. It sought to acquire now-defunct carrier Spirit Airlines, but that deal was upended by a federal judge who ruled it was anticompetitive. A judge also blocked a regional partnership between JetBlue and American Airlines , which the airlines argued would help them compete better against carriers in the congested Northeast U.S. JetBlue now has a partnership with United Airlines . headlines.summary: Coca-Cola stock has climbed about 32% so far this year, raising the beverage company's market cap to roughly $398 billion.
headlines.article_text: Coca-Cola (KO) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Coca-Cola topped Wall Street's estimates for its quarterly earnings and revenue. The company hiked its full-year forecast for the third straight quarter. In this article KO Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Multipacks of Coca-Cola Original Taste glass bottles, 4x200ml, line a supermarket shelf in Bari, Italy, on September 15, 2026. Matteo Della Torre | Nurphoto | Getty Images Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its full-year outlook for the third straight quarter, despite lackluster demand in its home market. For the full year, Coke now expects comparable earnings per share to grow at least 11%, up from its prior forecast of an increase in the range of 9% to 10%. The beverage giant also anticipates that its organic revenue will climb at least 5%, a slight increase from its previous outlook of approximately 5% growth. Shares of the company rose about 1% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported compared with what Wall Street analysts surveyed by LSEG were expecting: Earnings per share: 91 cents adjusted vs. 88 cents expected Revenue: $13.4 billion vs. $12.92 billion expected Coke reported third-quarter net income attributable to shareholders of $4.01 billion, or 93 cents per share, up from $3.7 billion, or 86 cents per share, a year earlier. Excluding transaction gains and other items, Coke earned 91 cents per share. Net sales rose 7% to $13.4 billion. Coke's organic revenue, which strips out acquisitions, divestitures and foreign currency, also rose 7% in the quarter. For the second straight quarter, the company's unit case volume increased 5%, helped by higher demand outside of North America. Coke's home market reported flat volume. However, the company's North American business would have reported volume growth if not for the timing of the Fourth of July holiday and the months-long shortage of Topo Chico, a sparkling water brand Coke owns, CFO John Murphy told CNBC. "The underlying momentum remains quite strong," he said. "Consumer sentiment is largely unchanged in the sense that, wherever you are on the income scale, you're looking for value, and I think our system here has done a good job interpreting that." In recent quarters, Coke executives have said North American shoppers are under pressure, stretched thin by inflation and economic uncertainty. But the beverage giant has also said consumers are still buying its drinks, from premium brands like Fairlife to its namesake soda. Globally, Coke's sparkling soft drinks business saw volume increase 5% during the quarter, lifted by growth of Coke, Coke Zero Sugar and Diet Coke. Diet Coke is having a "resurgence," Murphy said. Gen Z consumers in the U.S. have nicknamed it a "fridge cigarette," while consumers in India threw Diet Coke parties as shortages tied to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran have made the drink scarce. "It's a brand that's almost reinventing itself with the next generation of consumers," he said. Coke has also gained market share as rival PepsiCo sees its soda business struggle, according to Murphy. Still, some of Coke's soda brands, like Sprite, have "some work to do." Coke's water, sports, coffee and tea division also saw volume climb by 5%. Increased demand for its water, which includes its premium Smartwater brand, fueled the growth. Demand for its tea and coffee was flat, while sports drinks declined. The company's juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverages business reported flat volume, despite growth in brands like Fairlife and Minute Maid. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: PYPL, GLW, UPS, KO Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making headlines before the bell: PayPal — Shares slipped 1% after the digital payments platform reported a revenue miss in its third-quarter report. The company reported revenue of $8.58 billion, compared to an LSEG estimate of $8.71 billion. Earnings, however, beat estimates and PayPal raised its full-year profit forecast. Corning — The materials science stock popped nearly 3% on third-quarter results that exceeded expectations. Corning reported earnings of 91 cents per share, excluding items, on revenue of $5.08 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected per-share earnings of 88 cents on revenues of $5.02 billion. UPS — The package delivery company gained 1.6% after it reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance. UPS projects full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion. Coca-Cola — Shares of the beverage giant gained 0.3% after Coca-Cola said it raised its full-year outlook for a third straight quarter, in spite of lackluster demand in its home market. Coke expects comparable earnings per share to grow at least 11%, up from its prior forecast of an increase in the range of 9% to 10%. It also anticipates that its organic revenue will climb at least 5%, a slight increase from its previous outlook of approximately 5% growth. Nvidia , Meta Platforms — Nvidia said it will invest $3 billion in Meta after the social media and artificial intelligence giant announced plans to raise up to $95 billion to support its investments in AI infrastructure. Shares of Nvidia gained 0.7%, while Meta Platforms dipped 0.3%. Amkor Technology — Shares of the semiconductor packaging and testing company rose more than 3.5% despite the company missing analysts' third-quarter earnings and revenue expectations. Amkor reported earnings of 76 cents per share and revenue of $1.99 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected earnings of 78 cents per share and $2.04 billion in revenue. Amkor also reduced its capital expenditure outlook to around $2.5 billion for the fiscal year, versus prior guidance of between $2.5 billion and $3 billion. Royal Caribbean — Shares advanced 4.4% after the company reported third-quarter earnings that beat analyst expectations. The cruise line operator earned $6.57 per share, excluding certain items, topping a FactSet forecast of $6.38 per share. The company also raised its full-year earnings guidance for 2026. Boeing — The aerospace company was slightly higher by 0.5% after it reported mixed financials for the third-quarter . While it posted a loss that was wider than expected, revenue came in above an LSEG consensus. Whirlpool — The home appliance company tumbled 7% after reporting disappointing earnings and guidance. Whirlpool lost an adjusted 21 cents per share on revenue of $3.68 billion for its third quarter. Analysts were expecting adjusted earnings of 80 cents per share on revenue of $3.92 billion, per LSEG. The company also cut its full-year revenue guidance to $14.5 billion from $15 billion. It expects a full-year loss of $1.30 per share, versus the consensus estimate of a $1.55 per share profit. JetBlue Airways — The air carrier climbed more than 11% after JetBlue said it expects further margin expansion in the fourth quarter even as fuel prices are anticipated to be 85% higher than a year earlier. JetBlue reported an adjusted loss of 60 cents a share in the third quarter, compared to the 55-cent loss analysts polled by LSEG had sought. Revenue narrowly missed expectations, as well. Celestica — The supply chain management company surged nearly 15% after Celestica raised its full-year guidance. It anticipates adjusted earnings of $11.55 per share, up from its earlier call for $11.30 per share and beating the FactSet consensus forecast for $11.16. Cadence Design Systems — The electronic systems design company rose 1.8% after third-quarter results passed estimates and raised its full-year revenue growth outlook. Cadence Design earned $2.11 per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $1.63 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG sought $2.05 per share and $1.61 billion. — CNBC's Ananya Chetia, Michelle Fox, Davis Giangiulio, Fred Imbert, Paulina Likos, Amelia Lucas, Darla Mercado, Laya Neelakandan and Kai Nicol-Schwarz contributed reporting
